enzyme_name: dTDP-4-keto-6-deoxyhexose reductase of the D-angolosamine pathway (Ang-ORF14)
organism_context: Streptomyces eurythermus angolamycin (ang) cluster; KEGG module M00803 dTDP-D-angolosamine biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG assigns R08927 (dTDP-3,4-dioxo-2,6-dideoxy-D-glucose -> dTDP-3-oxo-2,6-dideoxy-D-glucose, a C-4 ketoreduction) to ang-ORF14 (K19859), a gene whose pathway role was established only by heterologous expression of the ang cluster; the protein itself has never been assayed, and SDR-family deoxysugar ketoreductases of this type (e.g. the characterised SpnN) carry a single activity, so monofunctional is inferred rather than confirmed.
direction_note: ModelSEED keeps 2 H+ but no hydride donor; the NAD(P)H that makes this ketoreduction one-way toward angolosamine has been dropped, and KEGG itself tags R08927 'incomplete reaction'.

enzyme_name: dTDP-2,6-dideoxy-D-kanosamine transaminase (AngB; EvaB/MegDII/StaI family PLP aminotransferase)
organism_context: Streptomyces eurythermus ang cluster; homologues in the vancomycin/megalomicin/staurosporine deoxysugar pathways
rationale: KEGG assigns R08928 to K16436 (AngB), a PLP-dependent sugar-nucleotide 3-aminotransferase; the EvaB/MegDII family members are single-activity transaminases, but AngB itself has not been biochemically characterised, so the monofunctional call is inferred from family membership.
direction_note: The amino donor (glutamate) is absent from the equation, so nothing in it fixes a direction; PLP transamination is intrinsically near-reversible and is pulled toward kanosamine here only by the committed downstream N,N-dimethylation.

organism_context: Streptomyces eurythermus ang cluster (final step of dTDP-D-angolosamine biosynthesis)
rationale: KEGG assigns R08929 to AngMI (K13332), a SAM-dependent sugar-amine N,N-dimethyltransferase; it performs two successive methyl transfers but that is one catalytic activity iterated, not two distinct activities, so it stays monofunctional. The protein has not been assayed directly.
direction_note: Both SAM molecules and both SAH products are missing; KEGG flags the entry 'incomplete reaction (unidentified methyl-donors, possibly SAM)'. SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible toward angolosamine.

organism_context: Saccharopolyspora spinosa, spinosyn/TDP-D-forosamine pathway
rationale: SpnQ is a PMP-dependent C-3 dehydrase that needs a separate ferredoxin/ferredoxin-reductase (or flavodoxin) pair for turnover; the full in vitro account assigns the subsequent C-4 transamination to the separate protein SpnR, so for this reaction SpnQ acts with a single catalytic activity (an earlier report had ascribed a secondary 4-transaminase activity to SpnQ). Its redox partners are distinct polypeptides, not fused domains.
direction_note: KEGG's own R08930 is balanced with reduced ferredoxin, H+ and H2O; ModelSEED kept only the two sugar nucleotides, deleting the reductant that drives the deoxygenation irreversibly toward dTDP-4-oxo-2,3,6-trideoxy-D-glucose.

organism_context: Human/vertebrate liver; equivalent 5beta-reductase activities also occur in gut bacteria
rationale: The chemistry is 5beta-reduction of the Delta4-3-ketone of 11-dehydrocorticosterone to 21-hydroxy-5beta-pregnane-3,11,20-trione, the classic AKR1D1 reaction; AKR1D1 is a monomeric aldo-keto reductase with one NADPH-dependent catalytic site and no second activity.
direction_note: KEGG marks R08994 'incomplete reaction (unidentified donor)'; the NADPH that makes 5beta-reduction physiologically one-way has been dropped, so ModelSEED's '<' is reading a hydride-free stub.

organism_context: Clostridium scindens and related gut anaerobes (ThDP + Mn2+ dependent); human CYP17A1 17,20-lyase is a minor alternative route to 11beta-hydroxyandrostenedione
rationale: KEGG withdrew R08995 (HTTP 404) and replaced it with R13669, cortisol -> 11beta-hydroxyandrostenedione + glycolaldehyde, assigned to the bacterial steroid-17,20-desmolase encoded by the two genes desA and desB; that is a two-subunit ThDP enzyme carrying one catalytic activity, so under the multi-subunit exclusion it is monofunctional, not bifunctional. (If one instead credits human CYP17A1, that enzyme is genuinely bifunctional — 17alpha-hydroxylase plus 17,20-lyase — but it cleaves cortisol poorly and releases acetate, not glycolaldehyde.)
direction_note: The two-carbon co-product (glycolaldehyde) is missing entirely, which is why KEGG retired the entry; side-chain cleavage is an irreversible C-C lyase step, so synthesising cortisol from 11beta-hydroxyandrostenedione as ModelSEED's '<' implies does not happen.

organism_context: Plant; KEGG map00130 (ubiquinone and other terpenoid-quinone biosynthesis)
rationale: KEGG gives only 'EC 3.2.1.-, 4-hydroxybenzoate-O-glucosidase' with no gene, KO or characterised protein, and literature searches turned up no assigned enzyme, so the catalysing protein cannot be identified; the generic plant GH1 beta-glucosidases that would perform it are monofunctional but that is family-level inference, not evidence about this reaction.
direction_note: A glucohydrolase by definition runs hydrolytically; glycoside hydrolysis in bulk water is strongly exergonic and not reversed, so ModelSEED's '<' asks the enzyme to condense glucose onto 4-hydroxybenzoate, which is UDP-glucosyltransferase chemistry, not glucosidase chemistry.

organism_context: Plant; KEGG map00130 (ubiquinone and other terpenoid-quinone biosynthesis)
rationale: Same uncharacterised activity as rxn15907 — this is one of three ModelSEED anomer variants of the single KEGG reaction R09039 (here releasing beta-D-glucose, the anomer a retaining glycosidase would give); no specific protein is assigned in KEGG or the literature.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only direction a glucohydrolase runs; the reverse condensation would require an activated sugar donor.

organism_context: Plant; KEGG map00130 (ubiquinone and other terpenoid-quinone biosynthesis)
rationale: Third ModelSEED anomer variant of KEGG R09039, releasing alpha-D-glucose (an inverting glycosidase product); the anomer split is a ModelSEED expansion, not a KEGG distinction, and no catalysing protein has been identified for any of the three.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only direction a glucohydrolase runs; ModelSEED's '<' is the thermodynamically and enzymologically wrong sense.

organism_context: Nicotiana / pyridine alkaloid (anabasine, anatabine, nicotine) biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG R09051 carries the explicit comment 'enzyme not yet characterized' and no EC or KO, so the catalysing protein is unknown; the chemistry is simply loss of the C-3 carboxyl from 3,6-dihydronicotinic acid.
direction_note: The CO2 product is missing from the equation entirely; once restored, decarboxylation is irreversible and pathway flux runs toward the dihydropyridine, so ModelSEED's '<' (re-carboxylating with CO2 that the equation does not even contain) is untenable.

organism_context: Anoxygenic phototrophs — Rhodobacter sphaeroides, Chlorobaculum tepidum, Allochromatium vinosum
rationale: BchF is an integral-membrane hydratase that adds water across the C3-vinyl group to give the C3-(1-hydroxyethyl) group; in vitro it also runs the reverse dehydration and can epimerise at C3-1, but that is the same catalytic activity in reverse, not a second one. A R. sphaeroides bchF deletion accumulates 3-vinyl bacteriochlorophyll a, confirming the assignment.
direction_note: BchF is experimentally a reversible hydratase/dehydratase, so neither a hard '<' nor a hard '>' is right — but in vivo the biosynthetic flux is hydration (left-to-right as ModelSEED writes it, pulled on by BchC), so ModelSEED's dehydration-only '<' is the worse of the two calls; the IUBMB 'hydro-lyase' name is a nomenclature convention and almost certainly what pushed the direction the wrong way.

organism_context: Anoxygenic phototrophs; this is the chlorophyllide a substrate of the same BchF enzyme (KEGG R09059 / MetaCyc RXN-8785)
rationale: Same single-activity BchF hydratase as rxn15924, acting on chlorophyllide a rather than 3-vinyl bacteriochlorophyllide a; hydration and dehydration are one reversible activity on one polypeptide.
direction_note: Demonstrably reversible in vitro; physiological flux in bacteriochlorophyll a biosynthesis is hydration (ModelSEED's left-to-right), so the stored '<' points away from the biosynthetic direction.

enzyme_name: chlorophyllide a hydrolase / C-13(2) methylcarboxyl-removing enzyme (BciC), EC 3.1.1.100
organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum and other chlorosome-forming green bacteria; first committed step of bacteriochlorophyll c/d/e biosynthesis
rationale: A bciC (CT1077) deletion in C. tepidum cannot make BChl c and accumulates pheophorbides retaining the C-13(2)-methylcarboxyl group, identifying BciC as the enzyme; whether BciC catalyses only the methylester hydrolysis (with the decarboxylation following spontaneously) or both steps is explicitly left unresolved in that work, so a bifunctional esterase+decarboxylase cannot be excluded.
direction_note: KEGG's balanced R09061 is chlorophyllide a + H2O -> 3-vinylbacteriochlorophyllide d + methanol + CO2; ModelSEED kept only the two tetrapyrroles, deleting the water, methanol and CO2 that make the step irreversible and committed.

organism_context: Arabidopsis, rice, cucumber; the chlorophyll b -> chlorophyll a limb of the chlorophyll cycle
rationale: HCAR, identified genetically in Arabidopsis and crystallised, is a ferredoxin-dependent FAD/[4Fe-4S] reductase that converts 7-(1)-hydroxymethyl chlorophyll(ide) a to chlorophyll(ide) a; a single reductase active site, no second catalytic activity (its reported role in 'metabolic channeling' during senescence is an association/trafficking effect, not a second catalysis).
direction_note: The reduced ferredoxin that drives HCAR is absent, so the stored equation has no reductant; the enzyme only runs 7-hydroxymethyl -> chlorophyllide a (ModelSEED's left-to-right), making the recommended '<' the reverse of the only direction HCAR catalyses.

enzyme_name: uncharacterised ThDP-dependent acyl/pyruvate carboligase of the cathinone-ephedrine pathway
organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) and Ephedra spp.; MetaCyc PWY-5883 ephedrine biosynthesis / KEGG alkaloid map
rationale: No enzyme has been purified or assigned for the condensation of a benzoyl unit with pyruvate to give 1-phenyl-1,2-propanedione; only transcriptome-derived candidate genes exist for the khat/Ephedra amphetamine-alkaloid pathway, so the catalyst is genuinely unknown.
direction_note: The written equation does not balance (one oxygen and two negative charges short) and KEGG notes the benzoate 'may be thioesterified (benzoyl-CoA)'; a decarboxylative C-C coupling that expels CO2 only runs forward, so ModelSEED's '<' would require fixing CO2 onto a diketone.

organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) / Ephedra; MetaCyc PWY-5883
rationale: KEGG assigns only EC 2.6.1.- with no KO or gene; the transaminase that aminates pyruvophenone to (S)-cathinone has never been isolated, and the khat transcriptome work offers candidates only.
direction_note: The amino donor and its 2-oxo product are both absent, so the equation cannot encode a direction; pathway flux in the alkaloid-producing tissue runs toward cathinone, though the underlying transamination is intrinsically near-reversible.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme — branched-chain fatty acid synthase system (KAS/FabG/FabZ/FabI plus acyl-ACP thioesterase) of capsaicinoid biosynthesis
organism_context: Capsicum fruit placenta, capsaicinoid pathway
rationale: KEGG itself labels R09090 'multi-step reaction / fatty acid synthesis': three rounds of malonyl-CoA elongation on isobutyryl-CoA plus ketoreduction, dehydration, enoyl reduction and thioesterase release, carried out by the dissociated plant type II FAS; no single protein catalyses the entry, so the functionality question has no answer for it.
direction_note: Every NADPH, the released CoA and the three CO2 are missing as well as the enzymes being lumped; de novo fatty acid synthesis runs only in the biosynthetic sense, so '<' (degrading 8-methyl-6-nonenoate back to malonyl-CoA) is not a real process.

organism_context: Pseudomonas chlororaphis RW71 (1,2,3,4-tetrachlorobenzene mineralisation) and Pseudomonas sp. P51 tcb chlorocatechol pathway
rationale: Chloromuconate cycloisomerases are homo-octameric enolase-superfamily enzymes in which cycloisomerisation and the accompanying chloride elimination occur in a single catalytic cycle at one active site — one activity, not two; the tetrachloromuconate -> 2,3,5-trichlorodienelactone conversion was shown to be part of the induced chlorocatechol pathway in RW71.
direction_note: Catabolic flux is tetrachloromuconate -> trichlorodienelactone + chloride (metabolites identified in sequence in RW71); the chloride-eliminating cycloisomerisation is not reversed, so ModelSEED's '<' runs the degradation pathway backwards.

organism_context: Chlorocatechol branch of chlorobenzene degradation (2,4-dichloro-3-oxoadipate was identified as a metabolite in Pseudomonas chlororaphis RW71)
rationale: KEGG R09139 carries the comment 'unclear reaction' and is written as '2,4-dichloro-3-oxoadipate <=> CO2' with no EC, no KO and no second product; there is no enzyme to identify because the entry does not describe a chemical transformation.
direction_note: KEGG explicitly disowns the entry as unclear and the equation turns a C6 dichloro-oxoadipate into CO2 alone, so neither the ModelSEED nor the LLM direction is meaningful.

enzyme_name: sulfoacetaldehyde sulfurtransferase / coenzyme M synthase (ComF, methanogenesis marker metalloprotein 16), EC 2.8.1.17
organism_context: Methanogenic archaea — Methanocaldococcus jannaschii, Methanosarcina acetivorans (COG1900 family)
rationale: ComF/MMP16 replaces the aldehyde of sulfoacetaldehyde with a thiol to give coenzyme M, using a protein-persulfide sulfur donor and reduced ferredoxin; a Methanosarcina MMP16 deletion is a CoM auxotroph, confirming the single sulfurtransferase activity. The related COG1900 member L-ASST is a distinct protein, not a second domain.
direction_note: KEGG's R09153 is balanced with [protein]-S-sulfanyl-L-cysteine and 4 reduced ferredoxin; ModelSEED reduced it to 'sulfoacetaldehyde <=> CoM', deleting the sulfur donor and all four reducing equivalents that make CoM biosynthesis one-way.

enzyme_name: 1,1-dichloroethane reductive dehalogenase (TmrA / CfrA-DcrA family RdhA), EC 1.97.1.-
organism_context: Organohalide-respiring Dehalobacter spp. (e.g. strain UNSWDHB) and Desulfitobacterium
rationale: TmrA is a corrinoid/[4Fe-4S] reductive dehalogenase shown to dechlorinate 1,1-dichloroethane to chloroethane; it carries one reductive dehalogenation activity and associates with the separate membrane anchor RdhB, which under the multi-subunit exclusion does not make it bifunctional.
direction_note: The two electrons and their donor are absent from the equation; organohalide respiration only removes chloride, so '<' would mean re-chlorinating chloroethane, which this enzyme class cannot do.

organism_context: Cytochrome P450 route to trans-4,5-dihydrodiol pyrene in Mycobacterium vanbaalenii PYR-1 and in fungi (Crinipellis stipitaria, Pleurotus ostreatus)
rationale: KEGG gives only 'pyrene-4,5-epoxide hydrolase, EC 3.3.2.-' with no gene or KO, and the trans-dihydrodiol was identified as a metabolite rather than by assaying a purified enzyme; the answer genuinely forks by organism, since microsomal-type epoxide hydrolases are monofunctional whereas mammalian soluble epoxide hydrolase (EPHX2) is a true bifunctional enzyme with an N-terminal lipid phosphatase domain alongside the C-terminal hydrolase.
direction_note: Epoxide ring opening by water is strongly exergonic and is never reversed biologically, so '<' (dehydrating a trans-diol back to an arene oxide) is not a reaction any epoxide hydrolase performs.

organism_context: Pyrene catabolism in Mycobacterium vanbaalenii PYR-1 and related PAH degraders
rationale: KEGG annotates R09173 with the single comment 'non-enzymatic' and gives it no EC, KO or gene; the hydroquinone-to-quinone step is spontaneous air oxidation, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: KEGG disowns the step as non-enzymatic and the equation is also redox-unbalanced (2 H+ released with no electron acceptor shown); under aerobic conditions the autoxidation runs only toward the pyrenedione, so '<' is the wrong sense even as chemistry.

organism_context: Pyrene catabolism in Mycobacterium vanbaalenii PYR-1 and related PAH degraders
rationale: As for rxn16035, KEGG R09176 is annotated solely 'non-enzymatic' with no EC, KO or gene; this is the 1,8-isomer of the same spontaneous hydroquinone oxidation, so no enzyme exists to classify.
direction_note: Non-enzymatic per KEGG and redox-unbalanced as written (no oxidant for the two electrons); the spontaneous direction is toward pyrene-1,8-dione, against ModelSEED's '<'.

organism_context: Pyrene ring-cleavage branch in Mycobacterium vanbaalenii PYR-1
rationale: KEGG names the activity only as 'cis-4-(8-hydroxypyren-7-yl)-2-oxobut-3-enoate lyase' with EC 4.1.3.- and no gene or KO; the step is inferred from metabolites identified in M. vanbaalenii PYR-1 pyrene cultures and no protein has been isolated, so neither the identity nor the functionality of the catalyst is established (a spontaneous lactonisation has not been excluded).
direction_note: The equation is balanced, and a C-C lyase step that expels formate while closing the lactone runs only in the catabolic sense, so '<' would mean condensing formate back onto the lactone.
